narrative:
The model determined that you have a 26% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the level of savings you have. The short six-month duration you asked for actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval, as most approved applicants request much longer terms around 19 months. Unfortunately, this positive effect was outweighed by two negative factors.

Your checking account status of being overdrawn (<0 DM) pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Only about 13% of approved applicants are in this situation, while most have either positive balances or no checking account at all. Similarly, having no savings or an unknown savings balance also increased your risk score. This is fairly common (33% of approved applicants are in the same category), but in combination with the overdrawn account it signaled higher risk to the model.

Because the negative influences from your account status and lack of savings were stronger than the positive effect of the short loan duration, the overall prediction crossed the threshold for denial.

You should focus on building up savings and bringing your checking account into positive territory before reapplying. Even a modest positive balance could meaningfully improve your chances on a future application.
